pass_a_gloss: [...] you destroyed my land, and killed my people, you will not remain for the age of time, evil seed. Prepare your children to be slaughtered for the sins of your father, so that they may not rise up and inherit the land and fill the land with war, and I will rise up against them, says the Lord Sabaoth, and I will destroy their name and remnant and seed. The name of the Lord then, he says, will come through much time. And if someone should choose to understand historically, through seventy years God pitied Israel. But if he should go through the inward and hidden path of the thoughts, he will take into mind that the inventor of sin continued very much time, laying the yoke of his own perversity on all those on the earth, so as both to show them his own worshippers and to bind them in the nooses of sin. But the only-begotten Word of God appeared to us through much time, and there came the wrath burning with glory, and the oracle of his lips an oracle full of anger. For Cyrus son of Cambyses, God urging and raising [him] up to battle, made war on the [land] of the Chaldeans, and took by force the [land] of the Babylonians, and became to them as anger and fire, for he devoured all as it were, and having an unbearable attack, he was seen by those there like water dragging in a ravine, and he filled with uproar and confusion all the nations of the Chaldeans, condemned justly for vain error. For they thought, as I said, that even God being unwilling they overpowered Judaea. So the vain error took them. For the things from unmixed wrath were brought upon them by God, and they perished by their own impieties; and one might see the author-of-evil dragon having suffered this very thing. For the oracle of the Lord became to him an oracle full of anger. For they were being ordered to go off into the abyss, he and the wicked powers with him. And they have been consumed as also by fire, and as by much water being swept down by the power of the Spirit in the lowest recesses. For these too were troubled together for vain error. For he said that, The whole inhabited earth I will seize with the hand like a nest, and like eggs left behind I will lift, and there is none who will escape me or speak against me. And he thought that he is God in truth, and having transferred to himself the glory befitting the Creator of all alone, he considered he could rule continually over those on the earth. So they were troubled, condemned for vain error, and were taken by it. For penalty and wrath and punishment were brought on them, and for the sake of this cause. [Lemma, Isaiah 30:29:] Must you not always rejoice and go into my holy places always as keeping festival [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: “…you have destroyed My land and killed My people; you will not remain for ever, evil seed. Prepare your children to be slaughtered for the sins of your father, so that they may not rise up and inherit the land and fill the land with war. And I will rise up against them, says the Lord of hosts, and I will destroy their name and remnant and seed” (Isaiah 14:20-22).

So the name of the Lord, he says, will come after a long time (Isaiah 30:27). If someone chooses to understand this historically, God took pity on Israel after seventy years. But if he follows the inner and hidden path of the meanings, he will grasp that the inventor of sin went on for a very long time laying the yoke of his own perversity on all who are on the earth, so as to make them his own worshippers and to bind them fast in the snares of sin. But after a long time the only-begotten Word of God appeared to us, and then came “wrath burning with glory,” and “the oracle of His lips, an oracle full of wrath” (Isaiah 30:27).

For Cyrus son of Cambyses, with God urging him on and rousing him to battle, marched against the land of the Chaldeans and took the land of the Babylonians by force. He became to them like wrath and fire, for he all but devoured them all; and since his assault could not be withstood, he appeared to those there like water rushing in a ravine, and filled all the nations of the Chaldeans with uproar and confusion, for they were justly condemned for vain error. For they supposed, as I said, that they had overpowered Judea even against God's will. So vain error seized them. For the effects of unmixed wrath were brought upon them by God, and they perished through their own impieties.

One may see the dragon, the author of evil, suffering this very thing. For the oracle of the Lord became for him an oracle full of wrath. He and the wicked powers with him were commanded to depart into the abyss (Luke 8:31). They were consumed as by fire, and, as though swept away by much water, they were carried by the power of the Spirit into the lowest depths. For these too were thrown into confusion for vain error.

For he said: “I will seize the whole inhabited earth in my hand like a nest, and I will take it up like eggs that have been left, and there is no one who will escape me or speak against me” (Isaiah 10:14). He supposed that he was truly God; and transferring to himself the glory that befits the Creator of all alone, he thought he could rule for ever over those on the earth. So they were thrown into confusion, condemned for vain error, and they were seized by it. For judgment, wrath and punishment were brought upon them, and for this reason.
“Must you always rejoice, and always enter My holy places as though keeping festival…” (Isaiah 30:29).

choices.english: God took pity on Israel after seventy years
choices.why: κατελεέω is to pity; the seventy years end the captivity.
rejected: God destroyed Israel through seventy years

choices.why: The genitive gives the father's name; Cyrus is the subject.

choices.english: marched against the land of the Chaldeans
choices.why: καταστρατεύω with the genitive: to make war on.

choices.english: the dragon, the author of evil
choices.why: ἀρχέκακος, the beginner of evil; the devil as dragon.

choices.english: to bind them fast in the snares of sin
choices.why: βρόχος is a noose or snare; the verb is to bind fast.
